content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use there is and there are with singular and plural nouns. Model: “There is a table, and there are four chairs in the kitchen.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use there is and there are clearly and politely. One useful response is: “There is a table, and there are four chairs in the kitchen.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where there is and there are is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

exercises.prompt: Complete the natural sentence about there is and there are: There is a table, and there are _____ chairs in the kitchen.

correct_order: There is a table, and there
are four chairs in the kitchen
items: are four chairs in the kitchen

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about there is and there are.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.

language_focus: Use there is and there are with singular and plural nouns.
objectives: Use there is and there are with singular and plural nouns.
Use describing a room in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about there is and there are.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about there is and there are. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: How many lamps are there?
listening.transcript: There are two chairs by the window, but there is one lamp.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Contrast there IS and there ARE; make the final /z/ in is audible. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Contrast there IS and there ARE; make the final /z/ in is audible.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about there is and there are.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using there is and there are; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise there is and there are?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: There is a table, and there are four chairs in the kitchen.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about there is and there are with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about there is and there are. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: There is a table, and there are four chairs in the kitchen. Submit your draft first.
